title: CLI contracts: observe the real CLIs
description: Observe the official CLIs installed on the owner's machine (claude and codex are installed). --help and --version are free to use. Running real prompts consumes the owner's subscription quota: ask the owner first and keep prompts tiny. Never open credential or session files of any CLI. Document per CLI: how to detect it and its version, how to check login status without reading credentials, the headless/structured mode and its flags, the output stream format (save real samples as fixtures), how to resume a session, how to cancel, exit codes, how to isolate its configuration so several profiles coexist (environment variable or flag), and whether its interactive UI can be hosted in a pseudo-terminal. Record the minimum tested versions.
acceptance: docs/research/cli-contracts.md documents all of the above for Claude Code and Codex CLI
Real output samples are saved under internal/provider/testdata/ with no secrets or tokens
The document states which integration modes (structured, terminal) each CLI really supports and the minimum tested versions
The configuration isolation mechanism of each CLI is verified, not assumed

title: proc: supervised child processes
description: Implement internal/proc: start a child process from an explicit binary, arguments, working directory and exact environment; stream stdout and stderr line by line; keep a bounded ring buffer of recent output; report the exit code; and kill the whole process tree on cancel on every operating system (new process group on Unix, Job Object on Windows). Use only the standard library plus syscall; any new dependency needs an ADR.
acceptance: A process started with a context is killed with all its children when the context is cancelled, on Linux, macOS and Windows (CI)
The child receives exactly the environment it was given, nothing inherited
Output is delivered in order, line by line, without unbounded memory growth
A missing or non-executable binary produces a clear error that names the path
No goroutine or handle leaks after the process exits

title: Store: SQLite in WAL mode with migrations
description: Implement internal/store: create the data directory with owner-only permissions, open SQLite in WAL mode with foreign keys on using a pure-Go driver (no cgo), and apply ordered, idempotent migrations in transactions. Record the driver choice as an ADR (0005).
acceptance: The data directory layout in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is created on first open with owner-only permissions
Migrations apply in order, exactly once, and a failed migration leaves the database unchanged
The database opens in WAL mode with foreign keys enforced
go build with CGO_ENABLED=0 succeeds on every target

title: Provider interface, normalized events and contract suite
description: Define the Provider interface in internal/provider: detect the CLI (installed, version, supported modes, login status), start a session through internal/proc, stream normalized events (text delta, tool request, tool result, error, done), send input, cancel, close. Add a fake provider (a small test program that emits scripted output) and a reusable contract test suite that every adapter must pass. Finalize the interface section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
acceptance: The interface and event types are documented in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
A contract test suite runs against the fake provider and is reusable by adapters
Cancelling a session terminates the child process and its children
Events never include credentials or environment variables

title: Profiles: several subscriptions, isolated
description: Implement profiles in internal/provider: provider kind, CLI binary path, an isolated configuration directory under the data directory (using the CLI's own mechanism verified in P1-001), integration mode, terms flags and terms_checked_at. Detect login status through the CLI's own commands, never by opening credential files. A child process receives only an explicit allow-list of environment variables. There is no automatic switching or pooling of profiles: the API must not offer it.
acceptance: Two profiles of the same provider do not share any state or configuration directory
A profile stores no secrets; API keys, if any, are referenced from the operating system credential store
Login status is detected without reading credential or session files (tested with a canary file)
The environment passed to the CLI is exactly an allow-list
No function switches an employee's profile based on rate limits or errors

title: Claude Code adapter
description: Implement the Claude Code adapter in the modes enabled by the terms decision in docs/research/provider-terms.md. It launches the unmodified official binary, never alters headers or the user agent, never opens its credential files, and reports a missing, logged-out or too-old CLI with distinct, actionable errors. Use the recorded fixtures for tests.
acceptance: The adapter passes the provider contract suite in each enabled mode
Fixture-based tests parse real recorded output
A missing CLI, a logged-out CLI and an unsupported version produce three distinct errors
The adapter launches the binary exactly as installed and never opens credential files
Each mode is behind a capability flag with a terms_checked_at date

title: Codex CLI adapter and OpenAI-compatible API adapter
description: Implement the Codex CLI adapter (exec --json or app-server, as verified in P1-001) and a generic adapter for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured with the user's own API key, the fallback when a CLI is not allowed. API keys live in the operating system credential store, never in the database or logs.
acceptance: Both adapters pass the provider contract suite
The API adapter streams over HTTP and supports cancellation through the request context
API keys are read from and written to the operating system credential store only
Neither adapter opens credential or session files of any CLI

title: Workspace: per-employee folder and scrubbed environment
description: Implement internal/workspace: create each employee's working folder inside the data directory, reject any path that escapes it (including through symlinks and .. segments), build the allow-listed environment for a child process, and move deleted folders to the trash.
acceptance: An employee folder is created inside the data directory with owner-only permissions
Paths with .. or symlinks that escape the folder are rejected
The environment contains only allow-listed variables
Deleting an employee moves its folder to the trash, never removes it

title: Employees: model, storage and lifecycle
description: Define the employee (name, role, system prompt, profile, workspace folder, permissions), persist it, and implement create, list, update, pause, resume and delete in the orchestrator. Each employee is bound to exactly one profile. Deleting an employee keeps its audit log.
acceptance: Names are unique and validated
An employee is bound to exactly one existing profile
Pause and resume survive a daemon restart
Delete moves the folder to the trash and keeps the audit log

title: Sessions and turns: background CLI processes
description: Keep one supervised session per active employee alive in the background, independent of any client. Run turns, fan normalized events out to subscribers, persist the history, cancel immediately, and run many employees in parallel without one blocking another. Apply a restart policy with back-off for crashed sessions and resume sessions after a daemon restart through the CLI's own resume feature where it exists. Terminal-mode sessions are supervised the same way: they keep running without viewers, keep their replay buffer, and are restarted or marked as needing resume like structured ones.
acceptance: A session keeps running when every subscriber disconnects
Events arrive in order and are persisted to history
Cancel stops the turn and the process tree promptly and records the cancellation
A slow or stuck subscriber does not block other employees or the producer
A configurable concurrency limit queues extra turns instead of failing
A crashing CLI is restarted with back-off and gives up with a clear error
After a daemon restart, sessions are resumed or marked as needing resume
Terminal-mode sessions also survive having no viewer and expose replay to the next one

title: Permissions, approvals and audit log
description: Classify actions (run command, write outside the folder, network access, read outside the folder), ask the user for approval through the API, remember decisions per employee, and write an append-only audit log.
acceptance: Sensitive actions are denied by default until approved
A remembered decision applies only to the employee and action it was given for
The audit log is append-only: the code exposes no update or delete of audit rows
An approval request that times out is a denial

title: Employee memory: SQLite plus Markdown notes
description: Give every employee persistent memory: structured facts in SQLite and free notes as Markdown files in its folder, with full-text search across both. One employee can never read another's memory.
acceptance: Notes are plain Markdown files the user can edit by hand, and edits are picked up
Search finds facts and notes using SQLite full-text search
Memory is isolated per employee, enforced by tests
Memory survives a profile or provider change

title: Daemon lifecycle and local network access
description: Make the daemon behave as a background program on a personal PC. internal/lifecycle: single-instance lock (a stale lock is reclaimed), a discovery file with address, pid and start time (owner-only), and autostart at login on Windows, macOS and Linux. internal/netaccess: listen on loopback only, generate a local token with owner-only permissions, refuse any non-loopback bind. Graceful shutdown stops all sessions.
acceptance: A second daemon instance exits with a clear message pointing to the running one
A stale lock left by a crashed daemon is reclaimed
The discovery file and the token are owner-only
Binding to a non-loopback address is refused
Autostart can be enabled and disabled on each operating system

title: API: HTTP and WebSocket with authentication
description: Expose profiles, employees, sessions, turns, approvals and memory over HTTP and WebSocket on loopback. Every request needs the local token, WebSocket origins are validated, CORS is closed. Document the API in docs/API.md; it is the only contract with clients. Terminal-mode sessions stream their bytes over a binary WebSocket with replay on attach, accept input and resize.
acceptance: Requests without a valid token are rejected
A WebSocket upgrade from a foreign origin is rejected, so a web page cannot talk to the local daemon
A turn streams over WebSocket and can be cancelled from the client
Approval requests and answers work over the API
docs/API.md lists every endpoint and event
A terminal session can be attached, resized and written to over the API, receiving replay first

title: Go client and the aotus command
description: Build internal/client (discover the running daemon through the discovery file, authenticate, call the API, stream events) and cmd/aotus on top of it for development, tests and headless use: status, profiles, employees, chat, approvals. Neither imports daemon internals.
acceptance: The client finds a running daemon through the discovery file
List, create, pause and delete employees; chat with streaming; answer approvals
The architecture check proves the client and the command import only internal/client and internal/version

title: Desktop stack spike: Wails version and frontend framework
description: Prototype a window and a tray entry that talks to the daemon, with Wails v2 and with Wails v3 (beta), and a minimal chat list in Svelte and in Preact (TypeScript). Prerequisites on the machine: a C compiler, Node, and on Linux the WebKitGTK development packages (on Fedora, webkit2gtk4.1-devel). Measure memory of the window with a long message history, check the tray, check behavior on the Linux distributions we target, and judge stability. Record the result in docs/research/desktop-spike.md and decide in ADR 0010.
acceptance: docs/research/desktop-spike.md compares Wails v2 and v3 on tray, Linux support, stability and memory with measured numbers
It compares Svelte and Preact on size, memory with 1000 messages and effort
ADR 0010 decides the Wails version and the frontend framework and states the native build prerequisites per operating system
The spike code is not merged into product packages

title: Desktop app: window, tray, employees, chat and approvals
description: Build cmd/aotus-desktop (build tag desktop) with the stack decided in ADR 0010: Wails v3 (gtk3 tag on Linux) and a Svelte frontend. The Go side of the app uses internal/client and exposes typed methods and events to the frontend; the token never reaches the WebView. On start it finds a running daemon through the discovery file or starts aotusd; closing the window quits the app by default (only the daemon stays), with a setting to keep it in the tray. Screens: profiles (link a subscription, see login status, run the in-profile login), employee list, create employee, chat with streaming and cancel, terminal view (xterm.js), approvals, history. Keep memory low: virtualized message list, history loaded on demand, incremental streaming. Record the memory of the window with a 1000-message history in docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
acceptance: The app reuses a running daemon or starts one, and never embeds it
Closing the window quits the app and leaves the daemon and its sessions running; with the tray option on, a tray entry reopens the window
A user can link a profile, log it in, create an employee, chat with streaming, cancel, answer approvals and use a terminal-mode employee
The frontend never receives the token and never calls the daemon directly
Long histories are virtualized and loaded on demand; memory with 1000 messages is measured and recorded in docs/BENCHMARKS.md
The app builds with go build -tags desktop on Linux (gtk3 tag), macOS and Windows

title: Packaging and CI on every operating system
description: CI matrix that runs the tests and builds the desktop app natively on ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners and cross-builds the daemon for the five targets without cgo. Release workflow producing installers or portable packages per operating system (the Wails packaging output), with the version injected through ldflags. Write docs/QUICKSTART.md covering native prerequisites.
acceptance: CI runs the tests on ubuntu, macos and windows runners and builds the desktop app with -tags desktop on each
The daemon cross-builds for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64 with CGO_ENABLED=0
A release workflow produces a package per operating system
docs/QUICKSTART.md takes a new user from download to a working employee
Release binaries report their version

title: Performance budgets as tests
description: Turn the performance budgets into automated tests in internal/bench and record the measured values in docs/BENCHMARKS.md. A budget that is exceeded fails the build. N2 and N3 are measured against a scripted fake CLI so subscription time is excluded.
acceptance: Each budget has a test that fails when exceeded
docs/BENCHMARKS.md has a table of measured values per platform
If measurements show a budget is unrealistic, the PRD and requirements.json are updated with the evidence instead of loosening the test silently

title: proc: pseudo-terminal hosting on Linux and macOS
description: Extend internal/proc so an interactive program (the official Claude Code or Codex UI) can run inside a pseudo-terminal that outlives any viewer: start with an initial size, keep a bounded replay buffer of recent output so a window opened later can redraw, fan the live output out to subscribers without ever blocking the program, accept input and resize, and kill the whole process tree on cancel. Uses a PTY library on Unix (an ADR is required: github.com/creack/pty is the candidate); Windows is task P1-021.
acceptance: A program started in a PTY sees a terminal (isatty) of the requested size, and a resize reaches it
Input written by the daemon reaches the program; its output reaches every subscriber
A subscriber that joins late receives the replay of recent output before live output
A slow or absent subscriber never blocks the program
Cancel kills the program and everything it started
The PTY library choice is recorded in ADR 0011

title: proc: pseudo-terminal on Windows (ConPTY), verified on Windows
description: Implement the same PTY API of P1-020 on Windows with ConPTY, assigning the program to the Job Object so cancel kills its whole tree. This could not be run where the project is developed (Linux), so the task is finished only with evidence from a real Windows 10/11 machine or the Windows CI runner: run go test ./internal/proc -run TestPTY -v there and paste the result and the OS version into docs/research/windows-verification.md. The same document records any other Windows-only check found by earlier tasks (Job Object tree kill in internal/proc, autostart in internal/lifecycle).
acceptance: The PTY tests of P1-020 pass on Windows with ConPTY
Cancel kills the whole tree on Windows (Job Object), including the existing proc tests
docs/research/windows-verification.md holds the command output and the Windows version it ran on

title: Terminal-mode sessions and in-profile login for Claude Code and Codex
description: Add ModeTerminal to the Claude Code and Codex adapters on top of the PTY of internal/proc: the official interactive UI runs unmodified in a pseudo-terminal that the daemon keeps alive (resuming the provider session with the CLI's own flag when one is known), exposed through a TerminalSession (subscribe with replay, write, resize, interrupt, cancel). Also provide the login flow: run the CLI's own login command (claude auth login, codex login) in a terminal session with the profile's environment so the user signs in inside Aotus without Aotus ever seeing credentials. Claude Code's default mode is terminal (docs/research/provider-terms.md, Decision).
acceptance: Detect lists terminal mode, and a profile with no explicit mode uses terminal for Claude Code
A terminal session runs the unmodified binary with the profile environment and keeps running with no viewer attached
A viewer that joins later gets the replay, then live output; resize and input work
The login flow runs the CLI's own login command inside the profile and the profile's login status changes afterwards; the daemon never reads credentials
Interrupt types Ctrl+C into the terminal; cancel kills the tree
